messages:
support-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: hosted -> /v1/generate 503 spike detected for customer=acme-corp. 5xx rate +14% (5m window). sample request_id=rid_0ab12cd3. routing -> upstream pool infer-gpu-pool-1
anya: ack, taking this. collecting logs and core dumps. anyone oncall for infra?
sam: oncall. looking. initial question: is this same signature as last week?
mike: seems different. last week was worker OOM from large batch. this looks like segfault inside inference runtime right after kernel launch. stack shows SIGSEGV in libinfrun.so +0x1a3f. grabbing logs now.
anya: pasted tail of /var/log/infer-runner.log from node infer-node-42:
```
[2026-03-15T18:24:12Z] infer-runner[pid=3145]: loading model gpt-slim-4q-quantized
[2026-03-15T18:24:12Z] infer-runner[pid=3145]: kv-cache alloc ok
[2026-03-15T18:24:12Z] cuda: launching attention kernel, ptx_version=70
[2026-03-15T18:24:12Z] infer-runner[pid=3145]: runtime error: segfault at 0x0
[2026-03-15T18:24:12Z] infer-runner[pid=3145]: backtrace: 0x7f8a1c.. libinfrun.so::launch_attention()
[2026-03-15T18:24:12Z] infer-runner[pid=3145]: signal 11 (SIGSEGV) - sending coredump to /var/crash/infer-3145.core
```
anya: dmesg from same host shows GPU page fault and driver message:
```
[  496.123456] NVRM: GPU at 00000000:03:00.0: GPU reported page fault on address 0x7f8b000000
[  496.123459] NVRM: GPU lockup - switching to software recovery
[  496.123461] kernel: infer-runner[3145]: segfault at 0 ip 00007f8a1c001a3f sp 00007ffd6c3a7c80 error 4 in libinfrun.so[7f8a1c000000+120000]
```
sam: interestingly the CUDA driver version on that node is 12.1.0 but the quantized runtime was built with PTX target 7.5. mismatch could cause invalid PTX path. checking docker image tags.
jess: i can repro locally with a smaller dataset. repro steps below (use internal staging model):
```
curl -s -X POST https://staging-infer.run/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"gpt-slim-4q-quant","input":"hello","max_tokens":128,"batch_size":8}' -v
```
observed: immediate segfault in container within ~200ms for certain batch sizes (6-8). batch_size=1 works.
mike: that points to a kernel code path that only triggers when warps / blocks hit that size. could be a codegen bug in quantized attention kernels. also note the image was recently rolled with a new cuda toolkit build.
anya: mitigation options: 1) roll routing to non-quantized variant (gpt-slim-4) for at-risk customers, 2) add per-device max_concurrency limit to avoid high batch sizes, 3) cordon infer-node-42 and restart runners to collect fresh core dumps. which do we want now?
sam: do 1 + 3. route customer traffic to gpt-slim-4 and cordon the node. we should also add an automated config to route traffic to fallback_model when runtime fails with SIGSEGV.
anya: executing commands now:
```
kubectl patch svc infer-router -n hosted -p '{"spec": {"trafficShift": {"gpt-slim-4q-quant": 0, "gpt-slim-4": 1}}}'
kubectl cordon infer-node-42
kubectl drain infer-node-42 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data -n hosted
kubectl logs deploy/infer-runner -c infer -n hosted --since=1h | tee /tmp/infer-logs-42.txt
```
anya: results: routing patched, customer 503s dropped to baseline after 18s. cordon succeeded, container restarted and produced same coredump at /var/crash/infer-3160.core (collected).
infra-bot: coredump uploaded to s3://redwood-crashes/2026/03/15/infer-node-42/infer-3160.core (sha256: e3b0c442...).
jess: I'll take the core and run it through our local symbolizer and addr2line. initial mapping shows crash in attention kernel wrapper, and PTX error messages present in GPU logs.
mike: immediate patch idea: rebuild quantized runtime with PTX target 75 -> 70 fallback and test against driver 12.1 matrix. also check if nvcc used older ptx. might be that the kernel was JIT or embedded PTX incompatible with the installed driver.
anya: customer comms: support team, please send holding message: "We're aware of elevated 503s tied to quantized model variant and are routing traffic to an unaffected model. We're collecting crash dumps and expect a technical update in ~4 hours." tag acme-corp CSM.
sam: longer term action items: (A) add a runtime check at startup to validate driver/PTX compatibility and refuse to serve incompatible quantized models, (B) extend canary for quantized builds with batch-size stress tests, (C) add fallback policy in router to automatically switch to non-quantized model on SIGSEGV-like failures.
anya: creating incident ticket (INC-2026-1722) and assigning postmortem to eng-runtime + infra. I'll own immediate triage.
mike: for the postmortem we should include reproducible minimizer, exact docker image digest, kernel+driver versions, and the failing batch-size pattern. jess can you paste the symbolized stack once available?
jess: will attach /tmp/symbolized-3160.txt to the incident. early lines:
```
#0  0x7f8a1c001a3f in launch_attention(libargs*) at attention_kernel.cu:412
#1  0x7f8a1bff5f2e in run_infer_step at runner.cpp:1298
#2  0x7f8a1bfdb2c0 in http_request_handler at http_server.cpp:244
```
anya: good. adding temporary feature flag: runtime.disable_quantized_autoload = true for the hosted pool until we ship rebuilt kernels. rolling that via config now.

---

Action items / owners:
- anya: own incident, coordinate postmortem + timeline (ETA for technical update: 4h)
- jess: run symbolization, attach traces, add reproducer and batch-size minimizer (ETA 2h)
- mike: build & smoke-test quantized runtime with PTX fallback / different nvcc flags (ETA 24h for candidate)
- sam: update router fallback policy and add a quick health-check that triggers routing on worker SIGSEGV (ETA 6h)
- support-bot / support team: send holding message to CSM/ACME and update every 2h until resolved

Follow-ups:\n- verify no other nodes show same coredump pattern (infra to sweep all infer-nodes)
- add automated test for quantized kernels in CI that runs a small batch stress test on GPU driver matrix
- postmortem meeting scheduled: 2026-03-16 10:00 UTC

closing notes: most likely root cause = PTX/driver incompatibility combined with a codepath in quantized attention that is sensitive to batch shapes -> triggers segfault under certain batches. no evidence of intrinsic memory leak (not an OOM), but need to validate.
:eyes:
